title: A million words costs $50 from Anthropic and 87 cents from DeepSeek. Corporate America noticed.

content_html:
Roughly 750,000 words of AI output costs $50 if you buy it from Anthropic’s Fable. The same volume from DeepSeek’s V4-Pro costs about 87 cents, Fortune reported. Z.AI’s GLM-5.2 charges $4.40. Moonshot’s Kimi K3, pricey by Chinese standards, charges $15.

Corporate America has noticed. Companies spent a year competing to burn tokens. Now they shop for the cheapest model that can finish the job, the Wall Street Journal reported. The badge of honour used to be tokenmaxxing. The new one is thrift-maxxing.

The first response to the bills was rationing, when firms capped what staff could spend. The second is substitution, and it is a far bigger problem for OpenAI and Anthropic.

“It’s like driving a Lamborghini to go to the grocery store to pick up milk when that was designed to be raced around a track,” said Mike Saeks, a field chief technology officer at Cursor who advises companies on their AI returns.

He has the receipts. Cursor priced up building a web browser from scratch. Running the whole job on OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 cost a little over $10,000. Splitting it between Cursor’s own Composer model and Anthropic’s Opus 4.8 cost $1,339.

The orchestra, not the soloist

This is not companies abandoning American labs. It is companies demoting them to the parts of the job that justify the price.

Telnyx, which builds infrastructure for AI agents, ran 1,000 of them on a top Anthropic model under a $200-per-employee subscription. Then Anthropic stopped allowing third-party operating systems on subscriptions, treating it as a breach of its terms. Paying per use instead would have cost “like 100 grand per day”, chief executive David Casem told the Journal.

So Telnyx rebuilt the stack. Z.AI models now run its 1,400 agents. Anthropic’s Fable acts as the conductor and plans the work. Open-weight models handle the implementation. OpenAI’s Sol reviews what they produce.

The legal AI startup Harvey trained GLM-5.2 itself. It then gave the model a button to call Fable 5 when a task looks genuinely hard. “We work with all of them,” said president Gabe Pereyra. Zoom’s chief technology officer Xuedong Huang reached for an old Chinese story. In it, three ordinary people combine their wits to match one genius. That, he said, is the secret sauce.

“It really feels like a bloodbath”

The labs are reacting the way any supplier does when switching costs collapse. They are paying customers to stay.

“There’s zero loyalty that I’m seeing,” said Marty Kausas, chief executive of the customer support platform Pylon. “It really feels like a bloodbath right now.” Pylon has been handed months of unlimited free usage. Kausas reckons it has taken about $1.6m in free tokens from one vendor this year. Another gave $65,000, and a third gave $10,000.

Both labs say they are adapting. An OpenAI spokeswoman said GPT-5.6 Sol was trained to be far more token efficient. Anthropic released a powerful lower-cost model on Friday. An executive said customers can choose intelligence or price inside its own ecosystem. Both say they support open-weight models.

Why the gap is so wide

The price difference is not charity. Electricity costs less in China, and new data centres there meet less local resistance. Chinese firms are also willing to run thin margins to win share and become the default.

Export controls may have helped. Cut off from the best Nvidia chips, Chinese labs had to squeeze more out of worse hardware. “For the money [a Chinese AI company would] spend on an Nvidia chip, they can buy 10 local chips from Huawei or other local chipmakers,” George Chen of the Asia Group told Fortune.

From Coinbase to DoorDash

Household names are doing it too. Coinbase chief executive Brian Armstrong said in June that the exchange had halved its AI spending. It did so by pushing staff towards Kimi and Z.AI’s GLM models.

DoorDash sends what its chief technology officer Andy Fang calls “lower-level work” to Kimi, for “better quality [at] cheaper cost”. Airbnb has used Alibaba’s Qwen for customer service. Cursor built its own Composer 2 coding model on Kimi foundations.

The result shows up in usage. Chinese models took 57% of the tokens US firms consumed on OpenRouter during one week in July. At one point mid-month, all five of the marketplace’s top models were Chinese.

It reaches well beyond developers. IDC surveyed 260 decision-makers at US firms with more than 1,000 staff. Of those, 47% said they used a made-in-China model for at least one use case, The Daily Upside reported. One in five reported extensive use.

The IPO problem

Here is why this lands harder than an ordinary price war. OpenAI and Anthropic spent years racing to build the most capable models. Then they found that plenty of customers want basic ones. Both are preparing to list publicly. The Journal reports the shift is threatening the valuations they carry into those listings.

It also explains the lobbying. The fight over restricting Chinese open-weight models has run all month. It stretches from the startups opposing a ban to the giants who signed a letter defending open models on Friday. The price sheet is what that argument is actually about.

The market has already voted once. Moonshot announced K3 on 16 July. Nvidia lost almost $600bn in value and briefly ceded its place as the world’s most valuable company to Apple.

Reasons to keep your head

Not everyone thinks the sky is falling. On TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Sean O’Kane argued the industry does this every time. “We’re now a week out and I don’t think anybody’s feeling like the end is nigh like they were a week ago,” he said.

His colleague Kirsten Korosec asked the sharper question about a ban. “Are we accelerating and ensuring that Americans win the AI race, or are we ensuring that certain frontier labs do better than others?”

Real frictions remain. Gartner’s Igor Marchal warned about going public with it. Naming a Chinese model invites suspicion at best, he wrote, and reputational damage and procurement pushback at worst. Congress is probing Airbnb and Cursor over their use of such models.

The big clouds are also holding back. Amazon’s Bedrock, Microsoft’s Azure Foundry and Google’s Vertex AI still do not support these Chinese open-weight models. Bloomberg Intelligence analysts Mandeep Singh and William Tong made the point after their token-volume mix reached 68%, following the launches of K3 and GLM-5.2.

Today the weights land

Moonshot is due to publish K3’s weights for public download on Monday, Bloomberg reported. Anyone will be able to download, modify and host the model. Daily sales at the Beijing company have risen at least sixfold since K3 launched.

That date was always in the diary. When Moonshot unveiled K3 on 16 July, the weights were the missing proof, promised for 27 July. They arrive into a market that spent the intervening fortnight learning to shop around.

Sam Altman saw the mood shift coming. “This is the first year where AI spend has been a big topic,” the OpenAI chief executive told CNBC this month. “And all of a sudden, it’s a very big topic.”

content_html_zh:
如果你从 Anthropic’s Fable 购买大约 750,000 个单词的 AI 输出，价格为 50 美元。 据《财富》杂志报道，相同体积的 DeepSeek V4-Pro 售价约为 87 美分。 Z.AI 的 GLM-5.2 售价为 4.40 美元。 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3 按照中国标准来说价格昂贵，售价 15 美元。

美国企业界已经注意到了。 公司花了一年时间竞相销毁代币。 据《华尔街日报》报道，现在他们购买能够完成这项工作的最便宜的型号。 荣誉徽章曾经是tokenmaxxing。 新的模式是节俭最大化。

对这些法案的第一个反应是配给，即公司限制员工的支出。 第二个是替代，这对于 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 来说是一个更大的问题。

Cursor 的现场首席技术官迈克·萨克斯 (Mike Saeks) 表示：“这就像驾驶一辆兰博基尼去杂货店买牛奶，而这辆兰博基尼的设计目的是在赛道上比赛。”他为公司的人工智能回报提供建议。

他有收据。 Cursor 提高了从头开始构建 Web 浏览器的价格。 在 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.5 上运行整个工作的成本略高于 10,000 美元。 在 Cursor 自己的 Composer 模型和 Anthropic 的 Opus 4.8 之间拆分花费了 1,339 美元。

管弦乐队，而不是独奏者

这并不是公司放弃美国实验室。 正是公司将他们降职到了合理的工作岗位上。

Telnyx 为 AI 代理构建基础设施，在顶级 Anthropic 模型上运行了 1,000 个 AI 代理，每位员工订阅费用为 200 美元。 然后，Anthropic 停止允许第三方操作系统订阅，并将其视为违反其条款。 首席执行官 David Casem 告诉《华尔街日报》，按次付费将“每天花费 100 英镑”。

因此 Telnyx 重建了堆栈。 Z.AI 模型现在运行着 1,400 个代理。 《人择寓言》充当指挥并计划工作。 开放权重模型负责实施。 OpenAI 的 Sol 审查他们的产品。

合法的人工智能初创公司 Harvey 自己训练了 GLM-5.2。 然后，当任务看起来确实很困难时，它会为模型提供一个调用《神鬼寓言 5》的按钮。 “我们与他们所有人合作，”总裁加布·佩雷拉说。 Zoom 首席技术官黄学东讲述了一个中国古老的故事。 三个普通人结合自己的智慧来对抗一个天才。 他说，这就是秘诀。

“真的感觉就像一场血战”

当转换成本崩溃时，实验室的反应就像任何供应商一样。 他们付钱让顾客留下来。

客户支持平台 Pylon 的首席执行官马蒂·考萨斯 (Marty Kausas) 表示：“我看到忠诚度为零。” “现在真的感觉就像一场大屠杀。” Pylon 已获得数月的无限免费使用权。 Kausas 估计今年已从一家供应商处获得了约 160 万美元的免费代币。 另一位捐赠了 65,000 美元，第三位捐赠了 10,000 美元。

两个实验室都表示他们正在适应。 OpenAI 发言人表示，GPT-5.6 Sol 经过训练，具有更高的代币效率。 Anthropic 周五发布了一个强大的低成本模型。 一位高管表示，客户可以在自己的生态系统内选择情报或价格。 两者都表示他们支持开放重量模型。

为何差距如此之大

差价不是慈善。 中国的电力成本较低，而且新数据中心遇到的当地阻力也较小。 中国企业也愿意以微薄的利润来赢得市场份额并成为默认企业。

出口管制可能有所帮助。 由于无法获得最好的英伟达芯片，中国实验室不得不从更差的硬件中榨取更多的资源。 亚洲集团的乔治·陈 (George Chen) 告诉《财富》杂志：“（一家中国人工智能公司）花在 Nvidia 芯片上的钱，他们可以从华为或其他本地芯片制造商那里购买 10 块本地芯片。”

从 Coinbase 到 DoorDash

家喻户晓的名字也在这样做。 Coinbase 首席执行官布莱恩·阿姆斯特朗 (Brian Armstrong) 6 月份表示，该交易所已将人工智能支出减少了一半。 它通过推动员工采用 Kimi 和 Z.AI 的 GLM 模型来实现这一目标。

DoorDash 将其首席技术官 Andy Fang 所说的“较低级别的工作”发送给 Kimi，以“以更便宜的成本获得更好的质量”。 Airbnb 使用阿里巴巴的 Qwen 进行客户服务。 Cursor 在 Kimi 基础上构建了自己的 Composer 2 编码模型。

结果显示在使用中。 7 月份的一周内，中国模型占据了美国公司在 OpenRouter 上消耗的代币的 57%。 月中的某个时候，市场上所有五位顶级模特都是中国人。

它远远超出了开发人员的范围。 IDC 对员工超过 1,000 人的美国公司的 260 名决策者进行了调查。 据《Daily Upside》报道，其中 47% 的人表示，他们至少在一个用例中使用了中国制造的型号。 五分之一的人表示广泛使用。

首次公开募股问题

这就是为什么这比普通的价格战更难。 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 花费数年时间竞相构建最强大的模型。 然后他们发现很多顾客想要基本款。 两者都准备公开上市。 《华尔街日报》报道称，这一转变正在威胁到这些上市公司的估值。

它还解释了游说。 关于限制中国公开重量型号的争论已经持续了整个月。 从反对禁令的初创公司到周五签署捍卫开放模式信函的巨头。 价格表才是这场争论的真正内容。

市场已经投票过一次了。 Moonshot 于 7 月 16 日宣布推出 K3。 英伟达的市值损失了近 6000 亿美元，并一度将全球市值最高公司的地位拱手让给了苹果。

保持头脑冷静的理由

并不是每个人都认为天塌下来了。 在 TechCrunch 的股票播客中，肖恩·奥凯恩 (Sean O’Kane) 认为该行业每次都会这样做。 “现在已经过去一周了，我认为没有人像一周前那样感觉末日即将来临，”他说。

他的同事克尔斯滕·科罗塞克（Kirsten Korosec）提出了有关禁令的更尖锐的问题。 “我们是在加速并确保美国人赢得人工智能竞赛，还是在确保某些前沿实验室比其他实验室做得更好？”

真正的摩擦仍然存在。 Gartner 的 Igor Marchal 警告不要将其公开。 他写道，命名中国模式往好了说会招致怀疑，往坏了说会导致声誉受损和采购受阻。 国会正在调查 Airbnb 和 Cursor 使用此类模型的情况。

大云也挡住了。 亚马逊的 Bedrock、微软的 Azure Foundry 和谷歌的 Vertex AI 仍然不支持这些中国的开放权重模型。 彭博资讯 (Bloomberg Intelligence) 分析师 Mandeep Singh 和 William Tong 在 K3 和 GLM-5.2 推出后，其代币交易量组合达到 68% 后指出了这一点。

今天重量落地

据彭博社报道，Moonshot 将于周一发布 K3 的权重供公众下载。 任何人都可以下载、修改和托管该模型。 自 K3 推出以来，这家北京公司的日销售额至少增长了六倍。

那个日期一直在日记里。 当 Moonshot 于 7 月 16 日揭晓 K3 时，重量是缺失的证据，承诺在 7 月 27 日发布。 他们到达一个市场，花了两周的时间学习货比三家。

萨姆·奥尔特曼预见到情绪即将发生转变。 OpenAI 首席执行官本月对 CNBC 表示：“今年是人工智能支出成为大话题的第一年。” “突然间，这是一个非常大的话题。”
